chunks: My father (peace be upon him) narrated from Saad ibn Abdullah from Salamah ibn al-Khattab from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi from Maymun from Abd al-Muttalib ibn Ziyad from Aban ibn Taghlib from Ibn Abi Layla from Abd Allah ibn Ja'far, who raised it (to the Imam), saying:

Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever recites the Adhan and Iqamah, a row of angels prays behind him whose ends cannot be seen; and whoever recites the Iqamah, an angel prays behind him.'

key_terms.أَذَان: Adhan: The call to prayer announcing the time for salat.
key_terms.إِقَامَة: Iqamah: The second call to prayer, recited immediately before the prayer begins.
key_terms.صَفٌّ: Saff: A row or line, here referring to a row of angels.

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for reciting the Adhan and Iqamah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Thawab al-Amal, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam Ali (peace be upon him), highlighting the spiritual magnitude of the Adhan and Iqamah as acts that invite celestial witness. The narration specifies that reciting both results in a row of angels praying behind the reciter, whose extent is unknown, while reciting only the Iqamah brings a single angel. This underscores the unique status of the call to prayer in Shia tradition as a means of attracting divine presence and reward.
